recommendations.name: Standard Route
recommendations.summary: Fold this row into the Sitkum Glacier route on Glacier Peak and retire it, because the spire is only a landmark that climbers walk past on the way to Glacier Peak's summit, not a climb of its own.
recommendations.detail: Every account of this line (the route database's Sitkum Glacier page and two separate trip reports) describes the Sitkum Glacier route to Glacier Peak's main summit. Each mentions Sitkum Spire only as the landmark beside the ~9,500 ft saddle, and one winter party traversed below it without climbing it. No source documents an ascent of the spire, or the 'Class 4 / low 5th' finish, rappel, rack or 'under a dozen parties' figures this row gives it. The row's own beta goes to Glacier Peak's summit, its gain (8,500 ft) only fits the 10,541 ft summit, and a ~9,500 ft saddle cannot sit above a 9,355 ft spire. Those are all signs of two objectives fused into one row. Two things are worth carrying over to wa_glacier_peak_sitkum_glacier if that row lacks them: the current access facts (White Chuck Trail #643 inaccessible since the 2003 flood with no plans to restore; FR 23 closed at MP 3.7; the North Fork Sauk to PCT/White Pass/Red Pass to Sitkum Creek approach used instead) and the Boulder Basin climbers'-path detail. Everything spire-specific should be dropped.

recommendations.name: Southeast Slopes
recommendations.summary: Rename this route to 'East Slopes (via Airplane Lake)' and change its aspect and face from southeast to east; the route content itself is right.
recommendations.detail: Both first-hand accounts climb from Airplane Lake, which sits almost due east of the summit (the row's own pins put the lake at 48.0026,-121.0067 and the summit at 48.0018,-121.0233). One goes up the east slope and east face on snow and names the ridge as an alternative and a descent. The other scrambles from the lake to the ridge north of it, through a saddle with a class 3 rock ramp, then along the ridge to the summit. No source uses 'Southeast Slopes' or puts a saddle on a southeast ridge. The row's own itinerary already heads for 'the low point on the ridge east of the summit'. Change name, aspect (SE to E) and face ('East slopes and east ridge above Airplane Lake'), and replace the 'southeast ridge' wording in beta, pro_needs and the crowds note.

recommendations.name: Southwest Route
recommendations.summary: Rename this route to 'West Side (LeConte Glacier)'; the content already describes the west/northwest snow ramp and scramble, and only the name says southwest.
recommendations.detail: The peak's summary page says the summit is reached from the LeConte Glacier by a class 2/3 snow couloir and short rock scramble on the west side, with the 2-3 pitch low-fifth route on the east side, which is the sibling row. A 2020 trip report climbed a snow ramp on Old Guard's northwest side to a class 3 scramble, and a second report describes the snowfinger and class 3 scramble from the Sentinel/LeConte side. The row's aspect (NW), face ('West/northwest side, directly off the LeConte Glacier'), beta and pins already match. Only the stored name 'Southwest Route' disagrees, so rename it; nothing else needs to move.

recommendations.name: Deep Blue
recommendations.summary: Keep this route, but relabel it as a bolted sport route (not trad) on the tower's northeast face, and say the usual way down is a walk-off, with rappelling possible on a 70 m rope.
recommendations.detail: The route page lists Deep Blue as Sport/Alpine 5.13c, with a small cam set (.2-.75) and 16 draws, starting about 100 ft left of Vanishing Point. The tower's area page lists it as Sport and says the routes face northeast. The row's own overview, pro_needs and rack already say it is fully bolted and on the northeast face, so the labels are what is wrong: discipline 'trad' should be sport, aspect N should be NE, and face 'north face' should be 'northeast face'. On descent, the route page gives a 2.5-3 hour walk-off over the back of Mt. Baring as the usual way down, with a full rappel possible on a 70 m rope. The row's descent, descent_text and rappels fields say rappel-only with a 60 m rope, and should be rewritten to match. Both sources come from one publisher, so these changes rest on thinner evidence than the other routes.

recommendations.name: West Route
recommendations.summary: Keep this as the route from the Chiwawa River Trail up the old sheep path to Massie Lake and onto the west ridge, and rewrite the trip plan, which currently sends climbers the long way round through Buck Creek Pass.
recommendations.detail: The Chiwawa approach is well documented: about 3-4 miles up the Chiwawa River Trail to the 'M' tree, a ford, then the steep, unmaintained sheep-drive path to Massie Lake. The row's name, beta, approach, approach_variants, climbing_route, descent_text, bail and waypoints all already describe it. Only the itinerary, the timing breakdown and the partner fitness text describe the other approach: Buck Creek Trail to Buck Creek Pass, then a 'south basin' camp at 6,600 ft. That comes from a 2024 multi-peak loop that reached Massie's south basin by a different line. As written, the plan is also garbled: it goes 'past High Pass', which lies beyond Buck Creek Pass and away from Massie, and 27-29 miles does not match the row's own ~12.6 mile distance. Rewrite those fields for a Massie Lake camp. Separately, the Massie Lake elevation (4,800 vs ~6,600 ft in the row; the federal elevation service gives ~5,936 ft) needs one value. Both approaches start at the Trinity Trailhead, which the current Chiwawa Road closure cuts off either way, so the closure does not favour one approach over the other.
